answer: The routing module predicts boundaries between adjacent elements by calculating a similarity score [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 2]. The smoothing module interpolates representations using the router’s outputs to convert discrete chunks into interpolated representations, which attenuates the effect of uncertain boundaries and improves learnability [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 2][Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 3, §1 −'!"$][Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 6, §2.2.2 Dechunking]. The auxiliary loss is designed to target desired downsampling ratios [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, arXiv:2507.07955v2, PDF p. 2].
question: Dynamic chunking has to pick boundaries and still train with ordinary gradients. What do the routing module and the smoothing module each do, and what is the auxiliary loss for?
raw_answer: The routing module predicts boundaries between adjacent elements by calculating a similarity score [[cite:ba542a94ea6567d8]]. The smoothing module interpolates representations using the router’s outputs to convert discrete chunks into interpolated representations, which attenuates the effect of uncertain boundaries and improves learnability [[cite:ba542a94ea6567d8]][[cite:b442289c4f7e2e01]][[cite:5d11028ca85ca9d6]]. The auxiliary loss is designed to target desired downsampling ratios [[cite:ba542a94ea6567d8]].
